recent_posts.title: So You Want to Build an AI Agent?
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of building an AI agent in Laravel, starting from scratch. It covers creating an Artisan command, configuring the OpenAI API key in Laravel's environment and config files, making HTTP requests to the OpenAI Responses API using Laravel's HTTP facade, parsing the JSON response, making prompts dynamic with Laravel Prompts, and adding a CLI spinner for user feedback while waiting for responses.

recent_posts.title: Automate GitHub issue resolution with Claude AI agent overnight
recent_posts.summary: A demonstration of automating software development tasks using Claude AI agent to work through GitHub issues overnight. The tutorial shows how to create a bash script that fetches open issues, implements fixes, writes tests, runs formatters and test suites, and commits changes sequentially. It includes creating custom skills for the agent, implementing safety measures like iteration limits and dirty state checks, and using task tracking to avoid duplicate work across loops. The approach is particularly useful for personal projects where automated issue resolution can happen while you sleep.

recent_posts.title: Meet Bob. (And Then Build Your Own Bob.)
Accepting AI coding agents after initial resistance
recent_posts.summary: Jeffrey Wei reflects on how AI coding agents have fundamentally transformed his development workflow and business. While AI has devastated his educational platform's business model (forcing 40% staff cuts as developers need less traditional learning), he's personally experiencing unprecedented productivity and enjoyment in programming. He describes transitioning from writing code line-by-line to a developer-driven AI approach where he architects solutions and reviews agent-generated code. Despite initial resistance to this shift away from traditional coding, he's accepted that adaptation is necessary as AI represents a permanent change rather than a passing trend.

recent_posts.title: Reflecting on early programming screencasts and their technical limitations
recent_posts.summary: Jeffrey reflects on his early programming screencasts from 2013, acknowledging their poor quality due to limited resources and knowledge about video production at the time. He discusses technical constraints like YouTube's 320p resolution requiring oversized fonts, and admits to a lack of attention to detail. He suggests that being critical of past work indicates growth and improvement.

recent_posts.summary: Laracasts announces a Black Friday promotion offering 50% off their educational platform subscriptions. The announcement is presented in a creative noir detective story format, revealing the discount as the mystery's solution.

recent_posts.title: Running Clock - Laravel's AI Initiative with Ashley Hindle
recent_posts.summary: Interview with Ashley Hindle, creator of Laravel Boost, discussing AI integration in development workflows. Key insights include treating AI as a skill requiring practice, AI's role in code reviews (OpenAI's Codex reviews most PRs), and avoiding AI for initial project setup. Hindle highlights AI's value for decision-making and discovering Laravel features, while noting it struggles with Laravel-specific testing patterns. Recommends Claude Sonnet 4 for backend work and GPT-4 for frontend, and advises against "vibe coding" (accepting AI code without review).

recent_posts.title: What is a Single-Page Application (SPA)?
recent_posts.summary: Single-page applications (SPAs) load content dynamically using JavaScript instead of reloading entire pages like traditional web apps. They fetch only the needed content while keeping UI elements persistent, resulting in faster interactions and smaller payloads. However, SPAs face challenges with SEO due to their single-page nature and longer initial load times since resources are loaded upfront. Modern hybrid approaches combine traditional and SPA architectures to balance these tradeoffs.

recent_posts.title: Supercharged Search With Laravel and Typesense - 4 Hour Course
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive 4-hour course covering Typesense integration with Laravel. Starts with installation and basic setup, progresses through creating collections, importing data, performing searches, implementing filters and sorting, and building a search UI. Covers advanced features like faceting, semantic search, and vector queries. Includes practical examples using a books database and demonstrates how to handle queries, filters, and result ranking.

recent_posts.title: Why most programming job applications fail and how to stand out
recent_posts.summary: Most job applicants fail because they submit generic, template-based applications without reading job requirements or providing work samples. To stand out from dozens of applicants, candidates should: follow all instructions in job postings, submit actual examples of their work, write personalized applications that demonstrate understanding of the company, and create custom materials (like dedicated websites) showing how they can provide specific value. The key is treating job applications as a trade of value rather than just asking for employment, especially for small to medium-sized companies where hiring managers personally review applications.

top_posts.title: Laravel Gates in 120 Seconds
top_posts.summary: Laravel gates are used to control access within an application based on specific criteria, such as whether a user is an admin or an author. Creating a gate involves using the Gate facade and defining a closure that returns a boolean value. These gates can be applied in controllers, routes, and views to manage user permissions and access dynamically.

top_posts.title: Refactoring Laravel controllers to single action pattern for better code organization
top_posts.summary: Explores the concept of using single action controllers exclusively in Laravel applications, where each controller handles only one action instead of multiple CRUD operations. The author demonstrates refactoring a traditional resource controller into multiple single action controllers, discussing the benefits of improved code organization, better focus, and easier maintenance. While acknowledging the trade-off of increased file count, the approach enforces cleaner architecture by treating each controller action as an individual command, potentially leading to more maintainable codebases.

top_posts.title: Optimizing Single Page Application Performance with Code Splitting and Prefetching
top_posts.summary: Learn how code splitting and prefetching can optimize your single-page application's performance. By loading necessary modules only when required and prefetching others in the background, you can improve page load times and reduce latency for users as they navigate your site.
